¡New discovery at Chalkp'a!
Chalkp'a, now Camáchay , they had:
A City state for over a thousand years founded around the end of the 23rd century BCE, being after taht during the Atok invasions at the 15th century BCE one of the few cities taht did survived the invasion, after the Great Void, on the 11th century it founded the Workútupa Chalkp'a confederation,which later would led to the Chollp'ur empire and after it ended on the 10th century, the city would be abandoned, to be renovated on later Formative around the 6th Century BCE.
Contrary to older thought the city was completely abandoned however, recent explorations in the woods found a serie fortifications at south of Chalkp'a dating from 8th century BCE, while no known registries mention this place, in fact, no known direct mention of it remains.
"When the original worshippers of Kasaka(Chaska) had their city reconstructed under the name of Camáchay, they all returned from the most remote places to inhabit their old home[...]"
Múybuka was the name given by the archaeologists to the settlement, due it having fortifications carved on the stone, it seemed to act as a fortified settlement, despite impressive indeed, not much it was compared to other engineering wonders from it time, such as the Buccah taht was far more knowledged as the "best fortification on west", a serie of outposts of taht kind to defend against the "western savages" were also common .
The settlement had one of the most well preserved burials, with about 150 skeletons found , next to taht,  feathers of Condor and small tools of tin also found as offering, the funerary rites of the pre Classical people are a high mystery due to , not just the Wakeros (people who hunt ancient treasures, such as tombstone, palaces and ancient temples etc...only for treasures, they exist just as the idea of greed exist) sacks and just time passing.
"This a truly exciting found is, which only prove how much complex the funerary rituals were from so long ago..."
A single Khipu was also found, it meant the following:
"10 flutes of bone, 50 chisels of tin for 100 slingshots."
The site closed for studies will be for this time being, and later will be moved to the Museum of Camáchay.
they were lined up straight, lying on their backs, while being directly buried under the soil, without great ceremonies for most, few were found with the offerings mentioned.
